file_description: Field Shapes & Depth - Field boundary polygons and aggregated depth data
data_format: WIDE format - one row per field (static data)
use_case: GIS mapping, H3 spatial indexing, depth-based analysis, field boundary visualization

field_descriptions.field_id: Unique field identifier - matches field_id in production data for joining
field_descriptions.field_name: Official field name (yacimiento) - may contain multiple reservoirs
field_descriptions.reporting_company: Company that reported the data to government - may differ from operator
field_descriptions.operating_company: Current field operator - company responsible for operations
field_descriptions.depth_avg_m: Average well depth in meters - arithmetic mean of all wells in field. Proxy for reservoir depth and drilling cost.
field_descriptions.depth_min_m: Shallowest well total depth in field in meters - indicates shallowest target zone
field_descriptions.depth_max_m: Deepest well total depth in field in meters - indicates deepest target zone or exploration drilling
field_descriptions.field_boundary_geojson: Field boundary polygon in GeoJSON MultiPolygon format - defines areal extent of field for spatial analysis

depth_significance.shallow_fields: depth_avg_m < 1000m - Shallow conventional reservoirs, lower drilling costs, older producing areas. Common in Golfo San Jorge basin.
depth_significance.medium_depth: depth_avg_m 1000-2500m - Typical depth for many Argentina conventional fields. Moderate drilling costs.
depth_significance.deep_conventional: depth_avg_m 2500-4000m - Deep conventional targets. Higher costs, better reservoir quality often needed for economics.
depth_significance.unconventional_depth: depth_avg_m 2000-3500m - Vaca Muerta shale and other unconventional plays. Depth affects horizontal section placement.

geometry_usage.format: GeoJSON MultiPolygon - can contain multiple disconnected polygons for fields with separated areas
geometry_usage.polygon_structure: coordinates array: [[[lon, lat], [lon, lat], ...]] for each polygon ring
use_cases: Calculate field area (km2) using geospatial libraries
Generate H3 spatial indices for hierarchical indexing
Convert to WKT for database storage
Overlay with satellite data (flares, methane plumes)

depth_analysis.cost_proxy: Deeper fields generally have higher drilling and completion costs. depth_avg_m correlates with well cost.
depth_analysis.reservoir_pressure: Depth correlates with initial reservoir pressure (pore pressure gradient ~0.45-0.5 psi/ft or 10-11 kPa/m). Affects production mechanism.
depth_analysis.temperature: Geothermal gradient ~25-30°C/km. Temperature affects fluid viscosity, ESP performance, completion design.
depth_analysis.depth_range: depth_max_m - depth_min_m indicates vertical heterogeneity - multiple producing zones at different depths.
depth_analysis.unconventional_indicator: Vaca Muerta shale typically 2200-2900m depth. Fields in Neuquina basin at this depth likely target shale.

calculated_fields.field_area_km2: Calculate from geojson using geospatial library (shapely, geopandas)
calculated_fields.h3_index_res8: Generate H3 index at resolution 8 (~0.74 km2 hexagons) from centroid
calculated_fields.h3_index_res6: Generate H3 index at resolution 6 (~36 km2 hexagons) for regional analysis
calculated_fields.wkt_geometry: Convert GeoJSON to WKT format for database storage
calculated_fields.depth_category: Classify as shallow/medium/deep based on depth_avg_m

unit_notes.decimal_degrees: Geometry coordinates in WGS84 decimal degrees (longitude, latitude)
unit_notes.area_calculation: Use pyproj or geopandas to calculate area from WGS84 coordinates

data_integration.join_key: field_id - join to field production data on this key
data_integration.one_to_many: One field_shape record → many field_production_monthly records
data_integration.enrichment: Adds geometry, depth, and operating company to production time series
typical_workflow: 1. Load field production data (field-month time series)
3. Left join production to shapes on field_id
6. Export to Pyxis with geometry in WKT format

operating_vs_reporting_company.operating_company: Current field operator - responsible for daily operations, production, drilling. This is the company actively managing the field.
operating_vs_reporting_company.reporting_company: Company that reported data to government - may be working interest owner, operator, or designated reporter. Can differ from operator.
operating_vs_reporting_company.why_different: Joint ventures, farm-outs, or regulatory requirements may cause reporting company to differ from operator. Use operating_company for operational analysis.
operating_vs_reporting_company.data_quality: Operating company more reliable for current operations. Reporting company may be historical.

geometry_quality.precision: Polygons are government-defined field boundaries - may not match exact producing limits
geometry_quality.purpose: Administrative boundaries for regulation and reporting - not necessarily geological boundaries
geometry_quality.resolution: Boundaries may be simplified from detailed surveys - suitable for regional analysis, not detailed subsurface mapping
geometry_quality.updates: Field boundaries may change over time as fields are redefined, merged, or split. This is a snapshot.
geometry_quality.missing_geometry: Some fields may lack geometry data - newly defined fields or data gaps

technical_notes.vaca_muerta_identification: Neuquina basin fields with depth_avg_m 2200-2900m likely produce from Vaca Muerta shale
technical_notes.golfo_san_jorge_characteristics: Golfo San Jorge basin fields typically shallower (800-1800m), conventional reservoirs
technical_notes.depth_vs_age: Shallower fields often older, more mature production. Deeper fields may be newer developments or deeper pay zones.
technical_notes.multiple_zones: Large depth_range_m indicates multiple producing formations at different depths in same field
technical_notes.horizontal_well_depths: For horizontal wells, depth_avg_m represents landing depth + lateral section
technical_notes.geojson_multipolygon: MultiPolygon allows for non-contiguous field areas - some fields have separate producing areas

example_calculations.extract_centroid_python: from shapely.geometry import shape; geom = shape(geojson); centroid = geom.centroid; lat = centroid.y; lon = centroid.x
example_calculations.calculate_area_python: from shapely.geometry import shape; from pyproj import Geod; geom = shape(geojson); geod = Geod(ellps='WGS84'); area_m2, _ = geod.geometry_area_perimeter(geom); area_km2 = abs(area_m2) / 1e6
example_calculations.generate_h3_python: import h3; h3_index = h3.geo_to_h3(lat, lon, resolution=8)
example_calculations.convert_to_wkt_python: from shapely.geometry import shape; geom = shape(geojson); wkt = geom.wkt
